claims.statement: All six actions-sidebar groups (HoldingsGroup, IndicatorsGroup, PriceAlertsGroup, NotesGroup, DocumentsGroup, AIAnalysisGroup) are mounted only on the /security/[security_id] route and are not reused anywhere else in the frontend.

The actions-sidebar groups share a common shape: a Sidebar.Group with a GroupTitle (rotating chevron plus an optional action button) and a GroupContent rendering exactly one of four states — skeleton rows, SidebarError with a retry button, an inline empty message, or the list — while owning a bindable 'expanded' prop; the security page passes expanded={true} to all six so they start open.

The notes and documents groups treat a 404 from their list endpoints as an empty collection (no error card), while any other error sets a human-readable error message and clears the list, surfacing through SidebarError with a retry that calls the group's own refetch.

Notes CRUD is content-only from the client (SecurityNoteCreateRequest/SecurityNoteUpdateRequest carry a single 'content' string; 'title' is read-only), mutations re-run fetchNotes(), and deleting the note currently open in the view dialog also closes that dialog; create and update both trigger the asynchronous AI note-title Huey task.

The notes edit path is verb-mismatched: the backend exposes PUT /market/securities/{security_id}/notes/{note_id} but notesService.updateNote issues an HTTP PATCH, so note editing cannot currently succeed against this router while the create, delete and list paths match.

The AI-generated note title is rendered by the note list item, whose preview is 'note.title || first 100 characters of the content plus an ellipsis', so a note observed before the title task lands falls back to a content preview and later renders the generated title.

Document upload enforces a client-side contract in DocumentUploadDialog — allowed MIME types application/pdf, image/png, image/jpeg, image/jpg, text/plain and a 10 MiB maximum — rejecting a violating file locally without issuing a request; the accepted input extensions are .pdf,.png,.jpg,.jpeg,.txt.

Document uploads are written to the directory named by the backend 'upload_path' setting (default "data/uploads") under a uuid4-derived unique filename preserving the original extension, and the market_security_documents row stores the original filename, absolute file_path, file_size and client-reported file_type scoped to security_id plus user_id; deleting a document removes only the row, leaving the file on disk.

documentsService.downloadDocument targets GET /market/securities/{securityId}/documents/{documentId}/download, but no such route exists in the backend, so both the document list item's download button and the view dialog's preview fetch currently fail; documentsService.getDocuments returns a plain list (not a PaginatedResponse).

HoldingGroup fetches holdings itself and enriches them with portfolio share by calling accountService.getHoldings, accountClient.getAccounts, and then getAccountTotals for every account to compute portfolioPercentage = totalSecurityValue / totalPortfolioValue * 100; it suppresses the loading skeleton on refetch when holdings already exist and runs the fetch from an effect gated on expanded && effectiveSecurityId wrapped in untrack.

The security page independently loads holdings via accountService.getHoldings into its own 'holdings' state solely to feed blendedAverageCost / showAveragePrice into the chart's average-price line, so the same endpoint is read twice — once for the chart and once by the sidebar HoldingsGroup panel.

HoldingsModal accepts either a modalState or a plain bindable 'open' prop and only fetches holdings itself when the 'holdings' prop is undefined; on open it restores the holdings_period preference only when it is one of PERIODS (otherwise ALL), with a hasUserChangedPeriod flag preventing a late preference fetch from clobbering a user's period choice, and it persists a period selection fire-and-forget through patchPreferences.

IndicatorsGroup owns indicator preference state while the page owns compute-and-render state: loadPreferences calls onPreferencesLoaded so the page can apply chart style, timeframe and per-indicator settings (deferring onIndicatorToggle by 100 ms so chartRef is bound), and toggleIndicator assigns local state before the network await to avoid a lost-update race, persisting the whole indicators map before invoking onIndicatorToggle.

The indicator settings modal resolves the enabled flag from the persisted preference (preferences.indicators[id].enabled) rather than the page's indicatorConfigs because the page config is stale after a sidebar toggle; resetSettings restores color and numeric defaults while deliberately preserving the enabled flag, updates the open modal's bound config so inputs reflect the restored values, and does not close the dialog.

Indicator compute requests carry interval and chart_style plus either the full active indicator set (refreshActiveIndicators) or a single spec (onIndicatorToggle), and include a 'candles' override sliced from the raw candles up to the rewind timeline position whenever the page is rewound; volume is computed locally from displayCandles rather than requested, and sequence counters discard stale responses.

PriceAlertsGroup receives the page's alerts array as a bindable prop and, when that prop is truthy, only mirrors it — never running its own getAlerts; only when the prop is absent does it fetch for itself while expanded.

The page owns alert mutation handlers used by both the panel and the chart: handleCreateAlert and handleDeleteAlert each call alertsService and then reload alerts, swallowing failures with a console error, so manual and chart-initiated creations land in the same alerts array that PriceAlertsGroup mirrors.

Elliott-wave drawing drives automatic price alerts through a serialized reconcile chain: ChartDrawingsService's onWaveAlertsReconcile routes to scheduleWaveAlertsReconcile, which chains onto a single promise so concurrent reconciles reading a stale alerts array cannot double-create; each run computes desired levels from wave settings, the current price and the drawn waves, deletes and creates wave-source alerts, reloads on change, and never propagates failure so drawing is never broken.

The initial-load wave-alert reconcile is gated on userPreferences being non-null so a failed preferences fetch can never mass-delete wave alerts, while a wave_settings change always triggers a reconcile.

AIAnalysisGroup is a pure launcher with three hard-coded actions (fundamentals -> analyzeFundamentals, summarize-notes -> summarizeNotes, portfolio-debate -> analyzePortfolioFit with the placeholder portfolio_context 'Analyzing in isolation for now.'); it owns no list state or preferences, opens AIResponseDialog in a loading state first, and fills content or error on the same ModalState while retry re-invokes the recorded actionId.

The AI response dialog's 'Save as Note' action creates a note through the same notesService.createNote call using the body 'AI Analysis ({title}):\n\n{content}', so an AI result becomes a note (and later acquires a generated title) without touching chart or note-group state.

On this route preference responsibility is split by key: the page reads chart_style, timeframe, chart_hide_labels, wave_settings and indicator_pane_heights and writes them from the toolbar and chart settings modal; the indicator group owns the 'indicators' map; the holdings modal owns holdings_period; and ChartDrawingsService owns elliott_waves and fibonacci_tools through setPreferences.

PATCH on user preferences replaces the whole value for a key, so the page always sends the complete object for wave_settings and indicator_pane_heights (the latter sending null to reset), while failed preference writes and alert mutations are caught and logged without user notification — only group load failures surface through SidebarError.

The security detail page's non-chart panels are pinned by a specific test set: page.server.test.ts asserts the load returns only security_id and never calls the market service, page.svelte.test.ts covers the instant shell, the in-page error card, the 401 seam, wave-alert reconcile and asynchronous indicators, the actions-sidebar holding-group and holdings-modal suites cover the panel and period preference, the indicator suites cover default restore and help modals, and tests/routers/test_documents.py covers upload plus list.

There are no dedicated vitest suites for the notes, documents, price-alert or AI actions-sidebar groups, and no backend test asserts the 404-is-empty client convention, so those behaviors are pinned only indirectly through the page suite.
